external_entities.name: colleague
external_entities.description: A colleague who signs in through the identity broker and uses applications.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Colleagues sign in to it from wherever they are, including their own devices at home.
external_entities.notes: The text does not state whether colleagues are asked for a second factor.

external_entities.name: franchise colleague
external_entities.description: A colleague from a franchise store who is vouched for by the franchise's identity provider.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Franchise colleagues do not have staff accounts with us; their own identity provider vouches for them
external_entities.notes: The text does not say which colleagues the franchise identity provider is allowed to vouch for.

external_entities.name: franchise store
external_entities.description: A franchise store whose colleagues are allowed to sign in through their own identity provider.
external_entities.source_excerpt: We also let the franchise stores in.

external_entities.name: franchise identity provider
external_entities.description: An identity provider operated by a franchise that vouches for franchise colleagues.
external_entities.source_excerpt: their own identity provider vouches for them
external_entities.notes: The text does not state which colleagues this provider is allowed to vouch for.

external_entities.name: HR system
external_entities.description: The system from which colleague group membership and leaver changes are pulled overnight.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Group membership is not maintained there by hand — it comes from the HR system overnight.

processes.name: identity broker
processes.description: Signs colleagues in, issues tokens, accepts federated sign-in, and provides token-signing public keys.
processes.source_excerpt: Everything colleagues use signs them in through one identity broker.
processes.notes: The broker uses one signing key for tokens for every application. Nothing calls back to the broker to ask whether a colleague is still allowed in.

processes.name: store admin console
processes.description: An application that uses token groups to authorize price changes and transaction voids for every store.
processes.source_excerpt: If the token has the store-manager group in it, the console lets the holder change prices and void transactions.
processes.notes: The console does not check which store the colleague belongs to, so a store-manager token works against every store.

data_stores.name: key store
data_stores.description: A store holding the signing key used by the identity broker.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The broker signs tokens with a signing key it keeps in a key store.

data_stores.name: directory
data_stores.description: The identity broker's directory of colleagues and their group memberships.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The broker keeps the colleagues and the groups they are in its own directory.
data_stores.notes: Nobody has written down whether the directory is encrypted where it sits.

data_stores.name: audit log
data_stores.description: A log to which the identity broker writes sign-ins.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The broker writes sign-ins to an audit log.
data_stores.notes: Nobody has written down what the log records or whether it covers the franchise route. Nobody has written down whether the log is encrypted where it sits.

data_flows.name: sign-in
data_flows.description: A colleague signs in through the identity broker.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Colleagues sign in to it from wherever they are, including their own devices at home.
data_flows.notes: The text does not state whether colleagues are asked for a second factor.

data_flows.name: federated sign-in
data_flows.description: The franchise identity provider vouches for a franchise colleague and the broker accepts that as a sign-in.
data_flows.source_excerpt: their own identity provider vouches for them and the broker takes that as a sign-in.
data_flows.notes: The text does not state which colleagues the provider is allowed to vouch for.

data_flows.name: issue token
data_flows.description: The identity broker issues a token to a signed-in colleague.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Once the broker has signed a colleague in it issues them a token.
data_flows.data_description: Token containing the colleague's staff id and group list

data_flows.name: administer store
data_flows.description: A colleague uses a token at the store admin console to change prices and void transactions.
data_flows.source_excerpt: If the token has the store-manager group in it, the console lets the holder change prices and void transactions.
data_flows.notes: The console does not check which store the colleague belongs to, so a store-manager token works against every store.
data_flows.data_description: Authorization token and price-change or transaction-void requests

data_flows.name: vouch colleague
data_flows.description: The franchise identity provider vouches for a franchise colleague to the identity broker.
data_flows.source_excerpt: their own identity provider vouches for them
data_flows.notes: The text does not state which colleagues the provider is allowed to vouch for.

data_flows.name: fetch public key
data_flows.description: The store admin console fetches the public half of the token-signing key from the identity broker.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Applications fetch the public half from the broker to check the signature.
data_flows.data_description: Public half of the token-signing key

data_flows.name: read signing key
data_flows.description: The identity broker reads the signing key it keeps in the key store.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker signs tokens with a signing key it keeps in a key store.

data_flows.name: update directory
data_flows.description: The identity broker maintains colleague and group membership records in its directory.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker keeps the colleagues and the groups they are in its own directory.

data_flows.name: pull changes
data_flows.description: The identity broker pulls group membership and leaver changes from the HR system overnight.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker pulls the changes once a night
data_flows.notes: The same overnight pull is how leavers stop being colleagues.

data_flows.name: write sign-ins
data_flows.description: The identity broker writes sign-in events to the audit log.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker writes sign-ins to an audit log.
data_flows.notes: The text does not state what the log records or whether it covers the franchise route.

trust_boundaries.name: corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: The corporate network where the identity broker and store admin console run.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The broker runs on the corporate network.

trust_boundaries.name: franchise identity provider
trust_boundaries.description: The trust zone controlled by the franchise identity provider and associated franchise identity environment.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: their own identity provider vouches for them
trust_boundaries.notes: The provider is described as belonging to the franchise rather than to the organisation.

assumptions.assumption: The directory is confidential because it contains colleagues and their group memberships, which identify or describe people.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the directory keeps colleagues and the groups they are in.

assumptions.assumption: The audit log is confidential because sign-in records identify or describe colleagues' authentication activity.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the broker writes sign-ins to the audit log.

assumptions.assumption: The key store is confidential because it holds the token-signing key, which is a secret.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the broker keeps a signing key in the key store.
